answer: Arrival-spacing barrier: a new identity’s first actions must follow a widening terrace of minimum inter-arrival gaps, and its rolling traffic cannot cluster tighter than that shape. Sybil batches arriving in lockstep get throttled into a slow spiral of retries, so each fake identity pays at least six hours of enforced delay before useful access. Repeated failures leave that identity on an island with no routing priority, so each retry costs more delay.
